description: SoorgaAI AI Maturity Stages Framework — 5 stages from AI Scramble to AI-Fueled Enterprise

stages.description: AI efforts are isolated experiments with no strategic direction. Individual teams may be exploring AI tools independently, but there is no organization-wide vision, governance, or budget. The risk is wasted spend and missed competitive opportunities.
characteristics: No formal AI strategy or roadmap
AI pilots are one-off and not connected to business goals
Data is siloed and not AI-ready
Leadership has low AI literacy
No AI governance or ethics framework
Workforce has minimal AI skills
Technology infrastructure is fragmented
stages.primaryRisk: Competitors with structured AI programs will outpace the organization within 12–18 months.
stages.nextStageTarget: AI Pivot — establish a clear AI vision and at least one funded strategic pilot

stages.tagline: Awareness is rising. First pilots underway.
stages.description: The organization recognizes AI's strategic importance and has launched initial pilots. However, these are often siloed within specific teams or departments. A cohesive strategy is beginning to form but lacks enterprise-wide alignment and execution discipline.
characteristics: AI strategy exists but is not fully funded or socialized
1–3 AI pilots running, mostly in IT or innovation teams
Data management practices improving but not centralized
Some leadership AI literacy — C-suite beginning to engage
Basic AI governance policies drafted
Targeted AI upskilling programs starting
Cloud infrastructure partially adopted
stages.primaryRisk: Pilot fatigue — pilots succeed in isolation but fail to scale, leading to disillusionment.
stages.nextStageTarget: AI Alignment — connect pilots to business KPIs and build cross-functional AI leadership

stages.tagline: Strategy is forming. Teams are collaborating.
stages.description: AI initiatives are increasingly aligned with business strategy. Cross-functional collaboration is growing, and repeatable processes for AI development and deployment are taking shape. The organization is transitioning from experimentation to disciplined execution.
characteristics: Documented AI strategy with executive sponsorship
AI Center of Excellence or equivalent team established
Data platform investments underway — single source of truth emerging
Leadership actively champions AI transformation
AI governance framework live and enforced
Formal AI talent acquisition and upskilling programs
Modern MLOps tools and cloud-native infrastructure
stages.primaryRisk: Speed — competitors who are further ahead may capture market share before full alignment is achieved.
stages.nextStageTarget: AI Transform — embed AI into core business processes and demonstrate measurable ROI

stages.description: AI is embedded into core business processes across multiple functions. The organization scales AI systematically with strong governance, measurable business impact, and a culture that embraces AI-driven decision-making. ROI from AI investments is clearly demonstrated.
characteristics: AI strategy is integrated into corporate strategy and investment planning
Multiple AI use cases in production delivering measurable ROI
Unified data platform with real-time analytics capabilities
C-suite makes AI-informed decisions regularly
Comprehensive AI governance with responsible AI practices
AI Centre of Excellence drives capability building across all functions
Scalable MLOps platform with automated model monitoring
stages.primaryRisk: Complacency — organizations at this stage must continue to innovate or fall behind emerging AI-native disruptors.
stages.nextStageTarget: AI-Fueled Enterprise — make AI a core competitive differentiator and drive industry leadership

stages.tagline: AI is the competitive core. Industry leading.
stages.description: AI is a core competitive differentiator. The organization continuously innovates with AI, operates with AI-first thinking across all functions, and sets industry benchmarks. AI capabilities are a key factor in attracting talent, winning customers, and entering new markets.
characteristics: AI is central to corporate strategy and competitive positioning
AI use cases span every business function — from product to supply chain to customer experience
AI-ready data infrastructure operating at enterprise scale with real-time capabilities
Board-level AI literacy — AI KPIs reported alongside financial KPIs
Industry-recognized responsible AI and governance frameworks
AI-first talent brand — the organization is known for AI capabilities
Proprietary AI platforms and models built on top of foundation models
stages.primaryRisk: Maintaining leadership requires continuous investment in next-generation AI capabilities and talent.
stages.nextStageTarget: Sustain and extend industry leadership through continuous AI innovation
